newsitem.title: ITALY: Italy's Scalfaro calls meeting on justice system.
newsitem.headline: Italy's Scalfaro calls meeting on justice system.

text.p: President Oscar Luigi Scalfaro called a special meeting with the speakers of parliament on Monday to discuss "grave issues" concerning Italy's embattled justice system.
Scalfaro said in a statement he would meet Luciano Violante and Nicola Mancino, the speakers of the lower and upper houses of parliament, for talks on Tuesday morning.
The meeting would evaluate "the grave issues concerning the judicial system...and give a proper outline of the problems connected to them", Scalfaro said.
He said the main issues, "both vital to democracy", were "the defence of fundamental human rights and the safeguarding of the autonomy and independence of the magistrature".

Many commentators have warned in recent weeks that the Italian justice system is in crisis, with magistrates probing other magistrates and political enemies using friendly prosecutors to fight their battles.

On Friday, police raided the homes and offices of Antonio Di Pietro, the former star magistrate of the "Clean Hands" graft probes, in an investigation into the methods he used to expose Italy's Tangentopoli (Bribesville) scandal.
Di Pietro, who resigned last month as public works minister, has called the probe "a joke and a vendetta".

Last week, reports leaked that a magistrate wanted to try centre-left Prime Minister Romano Prodi, a respected economist who took office six months ago with a pledge to renew Italy, for alleged malpractice when he ran state holding IRI.
